pairs.difference: A: the whole card is pulled warm. Yellow wall and orange deck planks fill the frame, and the anchor is a near-neutral dark grey with brown-black shadows in the lens (warm share 0.999, above the real range). Nothing cool rests the eye. B: an orange barrel set against a cyan sky, with cool steel bands that pick up a teal reflection in the lens. That is a clear warm hero against a cool background, like the real taxi and lawnmower cards.
pairs.fix: Put a cool background behind the anchor, such as a clear blue sky or blue-grey sea haze. Make the iron slightly blue-grey with cool reflections, and keep the deck wood a softer brown, not bright orange.

pairs.difference: A: the tan-orange money bag, gold coins and red cord stand against purple, a warm hero on a cool ground. B: a saturated blue machine on purple, both loud cool hues of similar chroma (warm share 0.026, below the real range). Only tiny can labels carry warm color, so the hero barely separates from the background by hue.
pairs.fix: Make the vending machine a warm color such as red or orange, or tone the purple background down to a soft lilac-grey. Fill the shelves with larger warm-colored cans.

pairs.difference: A: the dock and rowboat are pure saturated orange, and their shadows shift to red-brown, the generated habit of orange shadows everywhere. Saturated cyan water and green lily pads make the hero and background equally loud. B: the sails are near-neutral grey-white in the lens, the hull is a muted brown, and the sea is calm cyan. There are real neutral masses here.
pairs.fix: Paint the boat and dock as weathered grey-brown wood with a few warm highlights, not bright orange. Shade the hull in cool dark brown, and make the water a calmer, less saturated teal.

pairs.difference: B: a loud hot-pink wave background competes with a saturated green slide and a cyan ladder (background chroma 0.155, above the real range). The hero is no louder than the background, and only the white tiles are neutral. A: a blue snorkel on orange deck wood, a clean complementary split, with a transparent lens that shows deck color through it.
pairs.fix: Tone the pink background down to a soft muted pink or lilac so the green slide is the loudest thing on the card. Keep the pool tiles clean white.

pairs.difference: Both maps sit on similar orange wood, with blue sea and sand-yellow land. A has a red X and dotted path as its accent. B has a grey-steel magnifier and cream paper as its neutral rest. Chroma and warm share fall inside the real range on both, and on color neither card stands apart.

B: the green topiary stands on a green lawn in front of a green hedge, the same hue family for hero and background (warm share 0.046, hue families 3.13, both at the bottom edge of the real range). Only a pale stone ring and the blue sky break it up. A: green fronds against blue sky, with a brown trunk on warm sand and cyan sea, giving distinct hue roles.
pairs.fix: Set the green topiary against something of a different hue, such as warm beige paving, a terracotta pot or a pale blue sky over most of the frame. Make the lawn a duller yellow-green.

pairs.difference: B: the ship's wheel, post, rail and deck are all one orange-wood hue, and the wheel's shadows go deeper orange-red. The hero merges into the deck (hue families 2.73, below the real range), and the gold rim is the only accent. A: blue-steel binoculars on a pale blue-lavender city. The hues are close but the chroma is soft, with lots of near-neutral sky and rail.
pairs.fix: Paint the wheel in darker, richer brown wood so it stands apart from a lighter, greyer weathered deck. Shade with cool dark brown, not orange, and let more blue sea show behind it.

pairs.difference: A: a crimson background with pink rays, and inside the photo the magenta, purple and pink stage lights. The whole card collapses into one red-magenta family (hue families 1.91, below the real range), and the white frame is the only rest. B: a red buoy on a blue sea and sky, a warm hero on a cool ground. Its shadows go to a rich purple-maroon.
pairs.fix: Change the background behind the polaroid to a contrasting color such as teal or deep blue. Give the photo inside it a mix of warm and cool lights instead of all pink and magenta.

pairs.difference: B: four balloons, each a different pure hue (red, orange, teal, purple) at full chroma. It is a rainbow palette with no muted mass on the hero (hue families 5.45, above the real range). A: the parrot is also loud, but in an ordered red, yellow and green scheme against one blue sky.
pairs.fix: Limit the balloons to two or three related colors, such as red, coral and one teal, with softer pastel shading. Let the sky stay a calm, slightly hazy blue.

pairs.difference: A: the tricorn is a near-black mass whose shadows lose all hue (shadow chroma kept 0.111, far below the real range). Only the red feather and gold trim carry color against a loud cyan burst, so the hero is much duller than the background. B: a tan jacket with orange cuffs and a green sash on a green burst. Its shadows stay warm brown.
pairs.fix: Paint the hat in a deep navy or dark brown felt so its shadows keep some color. Add a soft blue-grey sheen on the top surfaces, and make the cyan background a little calmer.

pairs.difference: B: a brass lamp on a yellow-green burst with a glowing center. In the lens the lamp's olive-gold merges into the yellow-green rays, and the glass reads as background, so hero and ground share one hue family. A: a gold and red spyglass with a teal lens and dark brown leather on green. It has distinct hue roles but reads very hot (hue families 1.8, below the real range). On my vector this is close to a coin flip.
pairs.fix: Put the brass lamp on a background of a different hue, such as deep blue or teal, so the warm gold and flame stand out. Keep the glass chimney a cool, clear grey-blue.

pairs.difference: B: red velvet, orange-red planks, gold trim and coins, and warm sand. Nearly the whole card is warm, the cool sky is only a thin band, and the plank shadows shift to red-orange in the lens. A: the chest sits in cool blue water, its wood shadows go purple-brown, and the gold is offset by blue and pink gems and grey bubbles.
pairs.fix: Show more blue sky or sea behind the chest. Make the wood a deeper brown with cool dark shadows, not red-orange. Change the lid lining from red to a darker, less saturated maroon or navy.

pattern: Generated cards still pull everything warm and saturated: orange wood, cream instead of neutral white, and shadows that slide into orange or red. They also give the hero the same hue and loudness as the background (green on green, orange on orange, magenta on magenta), where real cards set a warm hero on a cool ground and leave some muted, near-neutral masses to rest the eye.
